03 / LOCALLY GROUNDED

Big possibilities.
Your boundaries.

Your best work shouldn’t need to leave your machine. Blue Nebula’s proposed foundation puts local storage and local inference first.

  • ↳
    Local by default

    A supported offline workflow, without a required cloud account.

  • ↳
    Permission with purpose

    Cloud requests and consequential actions get their own explicit scope.

  • ↳
    Knowledge you can own

    Inspectable memory, correction, deletion, and readable exports.

A LITTLE MORE CONTEXT

Good questions.
Clear answers.

What exactly is Blue Nebula?

Blue Nebula is the working name for a proposed local-first AI engineering workspace. It connects a repository, visual canvas, persistent project memory, local models, and visible verification. It is an application layer, rather than an operating system kernel.

Can I download the desktop app today?

This site presents the product vision and an interactive browser concept. A shipping desktop installer is not available here. The downloadable product brief explains the proposed scope, hardware assumptions, and roadmap.

Does this demo call an AI model?

No. The demo uses editable example data, deterministic workflow stages, generated JSX, and real local fixture checks. Everything in the demo runs in your browser. It does not index a repository, execute generated code, or connect to a local model.

Will my projects need a cloud connection?

The PRD proposes local storage and inference by default, with an offline supported workflow after installation. Optional remote providers and connectors would require explicit permission. These are product requirements awaiting implementation and qualification.

Which tools and machines are in the initial scope?

The proposed starting point is Windows 11 x64, VS Code, and React with TypeScript. A 32 GB RAM system with 12 GB NVIDIA VRAM is the proposed reference inference profile. A 16 GB CPU profile is best effort. Final compatibility and performance require trials.

How would memory and model training differ?

Project memory keeps inspectable facts outside model weights, where they can be corrected or deleted. Optional adapter training is a later, separately consented capability that would require reviewed data, evaluation, and rollback. Saving a memory does not train a model.
